question: Before the cut policy as it stands on main (r8: a result's tokens counted from its text, the proxy's breakpoint, tail pricing; thinking kept) goes out in a release: on every nine-turn task the bench has, what does a session cost, how many calls does it take and what does it pass with the cuts on, beside the same task run the same day with no proxy at all; and did each cut pay for itself by the end of its session?
rule: Chosen 2026-11-17 before the run, at the owner's ask for one larger benchmark before the release: every nine-turn task in bench/tasks (PostHog PR106936 and PR106672; MLflow PR26267, PR26269, PR26270, PR26300, PR26307, PR26311), none left out. Two arms paired by task, both run fresh: bare (straight to the API) and main-defaults (the shipped defaults behind a proxy of its own). One rep. PR26267 and PR26307 have no criteria and are judged by their check alone. A third arm added the same day while the first two were running, at the owner's ask, because whether thinking-cutting is safe to turn on is the question the benchmark was for: main-cut-thinking-older-than-2 is main-defaults with cutThinking on and thinkingKeepTurns 2: the two turns before the one in progress keep their thinking and only older thinking goes with a cut. The arm first started without the safeguard (thinkingKeepTurns 0) and was stopped two turns in at the owner's call; those sessions left no record. Same tasks, same model, one rep; its two lanes differ by the proxy's port alone.
